intro: A campaign for the family reunification of Palestinian refugees in Greece.
not_found_text: The address may have changed. Go back to the home page or sign the appeal.
footer_tagline: Because no one should be left behind.
home_hero_lede: A campaign for the family reunification of Palestinian refugees in Greece. Because no one should be left behind.
home_yes_text: For Palestinian refugee families in Greece, the authorities said “yes”. The reunion has still not happened, because the responsible ministries are not taking the next steps.
home_yes_right_text: The authorities have recognised the right to family reunification.
home_yes_minute_text: Sign the appeal and support the campaign.
home_yes_voice_text: Every signature adds pressure on the ministries.
home_quote_line_2: is for us to be together again,
about_story_lede: The story of a fellowship that began at a council and reached the far edge of Middle-earth.
about_team_lede: Nine set out from Rivendell. Six introduce themselves here; the rest are still on the road.
about_team_empty: The team will be introduced here soon.
about_story_opening: It all began at a council in Rivendell, when nine walkers decided that no one would go alone.
about_story_p1: In autumn we gathered beneath Elrond’s beeches. Elves, dwarves, men and hobbits, each with their own story and the same fear: that the road ahead was too long for one.
about_story_p2: A small hobbit stood up first. He did not know the way, he said, but he would find it. From that moment the quest stopped being one person’s burden and became everyone’s.
about_story_p3: We crossed mountains, mines and rivers. We got lost, we were scattered, we found each other again. We learned that fellowship is measured not in miles but in hands reaching out when someone falls.
about_story_p4: And when the journey ended, all we wanted was what every family wants: to go home and sit at the same table again.
issue_step_1_text: In a galaxy far, far away, the law of the Republic says that every family separated by war has the right to be together again.
issue_step_2_text: The application is filed at the office on Coruscant, in triplicate and stamped by the Senate.
issue_step_3_text: A council of protocol droids checks every document. C-3PO insists the odds are roughly 3,720 to 1.
issue_step_4_text: The answer is “yes”. The Force is with the family, at least on paper.
issue_step_5_text: Visas, tickets on the Millennium Falcon, a signal from the ministry. This is where the journey has to continue.
issue_step_6_text: The family lands in the same port, on the same planet, at the same table.
issue_what_lede: How the process should work, step by step, from the right itself to the moment a family is together again.
issue_stall_lede: After the “yes”, the jump to hyperspace never happens.
issue_stall_a_text: The Senate has said “yes”, but the visas sit in a drawer on Coruscant. Families hold a decision and wait for a ship that never comes.
issue_stall_b_text: Other applications have not even had an answer. They sit in the queue behind reports on Death Star repairs.
issue_stall_cost_title: What it means for the families
issue_stall_cost_text: Parents in different systems, children growing up with hologram messages, lives on hold. Every month of delay is another month apart.
issue_demands_lede: What we ask of the Senate, so the process is stitched back together where it was cut.
issue_demand_1_text: Anyone with a positive decision gets a visa within a clear deadline.
issue_demand_2_title: One office, one person in charge
issue_demand_2_text: A single point of contact at the ministry, instead of ten droids referring you to each other.
issue_demand_3_title: An answer for every waiting application
issue_demand_3_text: Every pending application is reviewed on a published timetable.
issue_demand_4_text: Every family knows which step it is on, without needing a Jedi to find out.
issue_strip_mended: Our demands stitch the process back together
